text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves letters, so this reading book is great for getting some practice in. I love that it covers what you’d expect with matching letters, but also includes other things like rhyming, what happens next themes, letters that start and end in certain sounds, as well as other concepts.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

The paper can also be used without the easel for painting, drawing and coloring.  It comes with bottles of paints in the primary colors which can easily be mixed to create other colors. The kit contains everything that your child needs to begin painting, except a drop cloth and an apron. Otherwise, you don't have to concern yourself with buying the items separately. There were some tears at first when a few of the tea cup towers toppled over, and I had to explain that’s why the game is challenging and it’s about practicing how to balance everything. Once we got over that hurdle, and a few extra practice rounds, we both just loved it!

There’s enough components to build 2 towers per face-off challenge—each side includes 1 flat thick cardboard tray, 4 plates and 4 cups (all of that x2 for the whole game). The card shows the order in which the tower needs to built for each round, and the first person to build it without it falling over dings the tea pot bell as the winner. The tea pot bell isn’t very pronounced in its sound, which is a good thing that it’s not too loud, but a little underwhelming when you’re excited to ring the bell when you win! It's just a charming design for a stacking and pattern recognition game, and it's definitely fun! Five stars!

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Mix BY HAND all ingredients, except flour and chips (mixing by hand makes them taste better, trust me).
Then add flour and chips and stir BY HAND. Bake @ 350 for 9-11 minutes on ungreased cookie sheet. Enjoy the preciouses.

text_fidelity_a:
Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers I absolutely love the concept of this little worker placement game, but the execution is not great.

You spend each turn doing basic worker placement stuff - go here, get resources, then convert those resources somewhere else, all while building a cell wall around your plant cell in an effort to turn your stuff into points. There is real science here - you use different cell components according to the actual chemical formulas of 6 water + 6CO2 to do photosynthesis, and cards are named after actual scientific stuff. There's also an area control segment of the board where you can earn some minor points and bonuses. The highlight, though, is that when you play this game, you'll know more about real-life science than when you started, and that's a pretty cool thing.

The game suffers though, because there just isn't much to do at the end of the game, and catching up is extremely difficult given that so few actions lead to points, and so many of the things you can collect are useful for only one or two functions. It's a little bit like saying that the science got in the way of the fun. When one person does the action to trigger the end of the game, there is usually a rush to do the singular action left that can generate points, and if you don't have it, you just stockpile some useless resources. That's a poor endgame, and on second or third playthoughs, you'll find that there are really only one or two viable strategies for winning at all.

Ultimately, this is an awesome game for teaching a small group of teenage scientists more about cell structures, but at the price of a hobby board game, it's tough to put in the hands of teachers for classroom use, and harder still to spend valuable class time to educate non-gamers about the intricacies of worker placement prior to their first play. And that play will run the course of a class period, more or less, so that has it's benefits, and it's detriments.

As a gamer's game, we found the concept extremely interesting, but the execution needed a little work. It won't hit the table often, because every other worker placement game we have is more exciting at the endgame, and offers us a greater variety of strategies for winning.

Do note that the addition of the "Mangrove" board, which was a kickstarter stretch goal, is essential to me keeping this one in our collection. The normal board is not nearly as good.
text_fidelity_b: Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers

The instructions are clearly presented by pictures and words. While the written instructions contain some useful learning information, it is possible for kids to put them together without fully comprehending the reasons why. That being said, the written instructions feel age appropriate and try not to over complicate things which is really nice.

As a teacher I plan on adding these to our STEM lab for our K-5 setting. My suggestion would be to start with project one and work sequentially. You don't have to (as my kid found out) but it's helpful. My kiddo routinely goes back to build and then explain why something works or doesn't. I never thought I'd hear my kid teach my about polarity!

Will be adding to our collection in the future. Well done!
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Jr. SC-100 Electronics Exploration Kit, Over 100 Projects, Full Color Project Manual, 28 Snap Circuits Parts, STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8 +

Abacus Brands Virtual Reality World Atlas - Illustrated Interactive VR Atlas and STEM Learning Activity Set This is a cool concept, and the app is easy enough to install and setup. I guess the only thing I was disappointed in, was that I was hoping to discover at least a few magical immersive experiences. Like visiting a pyramid in Egypt, for example. But instead, these are all short videos that have a broader and less immersive look into the different places. In Egypt for example, you visit Cairo and see pyramids, but you don’t get to see inside of the pyramids. The videos are all broad strokes of places or animals. Which I guess in some ways make sense, as it’s an atlas. However, it would have been so magical to at least have some really cool immersive experiences.

Overall, it’s a cool educational toy/gadget. But it could have been so much cooler, in my opinion.

TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad I’ve used the slide on a slight slope and almost a flat surface. PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. The splash zone edges (inflated) nearest to the slide don’t ensure participant won’t slide over and miss splash zone.
A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.

LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old LEGO have been hit by the inflation bug, and they've upped their prices recently on all sets. Nowhere is that more clear than in this set, which is very expensive for what you get.

Targeted towards the younger audience who is just beyond Duplo blocks, this is a pretty simple set with a pretty doofy-looking dragon that clearly skews younger, and doesn't fit in well with the rest of the Ninjago line, which is undoubtedly the LEGO line that has the highest "cool factor". So to judge this against a regular Ninjago set, this set woudl be a clear loser.

But it's really not for the older kids who can handle a ninja base or a 900-piece battle wagon, it's for littles. And for them, this is a fun set, but it is outrageously priced for what you get. It's essentially a few minifigs, a small dragon, a small set-piece, and a motorbike. Its simple to put together, but if you're working with a 4-year old, you probably need a little parental assistance.

For mini-munchkins, I suppose this would be a fun set to play with, but at close to $50 at the time of this writing, you are paying a very pretty penny for the fun you can have with it. At half that cost, and for the right audience, I'd find it a 4-star value. For what it is, I can't rank it higher than 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old

The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!

text_fidelity_a:
Chillafish BOX: Connectable Toy Storage and Play System, Blue/Red Love:
- The look.
- The stackability options.
- The strength of the outer cube (Brick).

Dislike:
- The storage bin section feels like it's a much weaker plastic than the rest - so much so that mine arrived with visible scratches and what looks to be either a flaw in the plastic or like someone pushed on it enough to not break it but start to weaken it.
- The cost ($49.99 at the time of this review) plus an additional $14.99 if you want the matching table top.

Neutral:
- The safety strap is rather difficult to attach to the cube because it is basically a really tight fit and has to push up inside the bottom slot and out through the upper slot. Not impossible but it'll take a few minutes.
- The size. Most storage cubes we have are a little bigger.

Optional:
- The table top is and additional / optional purchase. Because of the way the bricks are designed, the top does sit perfectly on top of the cube. There is nothing holding it in place, so it's probably not safe around young just starting to stand and grab onto things. It's easy to pull off.

Overall:
If these were just a little bigger or cheaper or both, we'd probably buy a bunch of them. As it is, I'll just have the one as a novelty near / on my desk. If you don't mind the price, these are probably fine. For me, the size difference + cost of many other storage systems just isn't worth it.

I obviously cannot review how well the work with other cubes as I only have one. but I really don't see that adding enough value to make me leave my more plain storage tubs.
text_fidelity_b: Chillafish BOX: Connectable Toy Storage and Play System, Blue/Red

text_fidelity_a:
VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys Oh, what have I done?

I bought Patrick the Pygmy Goat as a gift for my goat loving wife this past Christmas. Upon seeing it Christmas morning, her eyes lit up and she took to it immediately. I thought I had made the perfect choice.

Or so I thought.

I quickly found that it seems Patrick was always watching me. At night, he would sit atop the pillows on the bed watching over his new domain. Despite the fact his head seems to be affixed to only look to his left, it still seems he is looking at me no matter what side of the bed I’m on. When I tuck in my wife at night, he is there staring. When I come back from brushing my teeth, he is there staring. When I lift the sheets to turn over at night, he is there staring into my soul.

I’m pretty sure he is plotting against me. I can see him in the window looking down at me when I take the trash out to the street. I get phone calls with the sounds of capra aegagrus hircus breathing on the other end. Sometimes he is there under my feet when walking by or sitting on my chest when I wake.

I’ve spoken to my wife about my concerns, but she laughs them off. I’m starting to think she is in on it with the goat. With Patrick. Even now, he is watching me type.

Despite the above concerns, he appears to be a really great stuffed goat. My wife falls asleep with him in her arms each night as he whispers, whatever it is he is saying, into her ear.
text_fidelity_b: VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen Very educational with great building-blocks for math success. The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen

Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage I was disappointed in this microscope, BUT it is for preschoolers. Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

It comes with 24 slides, with 3 items on each one. (Plus one blank one.) There's an included book that tells what it is on each of the slides(page 27 and 28). There's no storage for these at all. It would have been nice for a container or bag of some sort to be included to hold all of these. For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. (It will only go one way.) There's a knob that turns on the front, and this will move the slide back and forth. That's it. There's no way to zoom in and out.

I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.
text_fidelity_b: Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage
